The core FLB phenomenon arises from behavioral biases in prediction markets: longshots (p < 0.10) yield lower-than-expected returns, while favorites (p ≥ 0.90) yield higher-than-expected returns. This is captured via terminal return per purchase, defined as r_f = (y_f - p_f)/p_f. The probability error E(A) = Σ q_f y_f/Σ q_f - Σ q_f p_f/Σ q_f measures how far observed outcomes deviate from market-implied expectations. Aggregated tail returns (R_TO) pool these returns across markets to assess systemic bias. These operators form a dual structure: one measuring outcome deviation, the other measuring expectation deviation. Failure modes include wash trading, early exits, and misinterpretation of hypothetical returns as actionable edges. The operators are sensitive to aggregation scheme: equal child-market weights, pooled purchases, or equal parent-event weights. Each reveals distinct aspects of market inefficiency. In GSE, these primitives enable dynamic calibration of longshot pricing and validation of de-vigged probability surfaces.
